item.title: Aaron Rodgers: Mike McCarthy fell asleep in meeting last week, broke down Steelers with "1-2-3 Packers"
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Rodgers's first comments since being benched by the Steelers came on The Pat McAfee Show.
item.content:encoded:
Aaron Rodgers made his first public comments since being benched by the Steelers on The Pat McAfee Show on Wednesday afternoon and they were very critical of head coach Mike McCarthy.

Rodgers said he did not hear the news of the quarterback change directly from McCarthy or anyone else on the coaching staff, but got the word from tight end Pat Freiermuth after it was announced on Tuesday night. Rodgers said that the change came after "months of conversation" about the offensive operation, including the playcalling, and that "things went to a different place" in recent days.

Rodgers said that McCarthy fell asleep in an quarterback meeting last Wednesday and missed other meetings leading into their loss to the Eagles on Sunday. Rodgers said McCarthy also broke down the team with "1-2-3 Packers" at halftime of that game and that McCarthy was not regularly watching film while preparing for games. Rodgers said he also believes McCarthy has lost the team in general.

"Everybody in that building knows the truth," Rodgers said.

Rodgers said similar things happened when the two men were with the Packers and that he believes McCarthy blames him for being fired in Green Bay after the 2018 season. He said he saw that McCarthy was not connecting with Steelers players early in training camp, but tried to help smooth things out.

"I protected him," Rodgers said. "I didn't talk about the things publicly. I didn't talk about his habits."

Rodgers also said he pushed to have changes made to the playcalling and game-planning that he believed were going to take place before Tuesday's benching pushed things in a different direction. Rodgers said that he told the team that if they weren't going to make those alterations that they should release him and said that there was no chance of a reconciliation with the team after how they handled things on Tuesday.

"That ship has sailed," Rodgers said.

The comments guarantee that Steelers players will be asked for their accounts of how things have been in the building since McCarthy's arrival this offseason and their responses will likely determine whether or not things go completely off the rails for the team in the final weeks of the season.

item.title: Dalton Kincaid, Christian Benford among five Bills listed as questionable
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Bills could be getting tight end Dalton Kincaid and cornerback Christian Benford back in the lineup on Thursday night.
item.content:encoded:
The Bills could be getting tight end Dalton Kincaid and cornerback Christian Benford back in the lineup on Thursday night.

Kincaid and Benford are listed as questionable to play against the Chiefs. Kincaid missed last Sunday's win over the Dolphins with thumb and ankle injuries while Benford sat out with a groin injury. Both players were limited participants in practice the last two days.

The Bills also listed defensive lineman TJ Sanders (shoulder), right guard O'Cyrus Torrance (ankle), and linebacker Dorian Williams (calf) as questionable for this week.

Every other player on the injury report was a full participant on Wednesday and no other players received injury designations.

item.title: Brandon Aiyuk agrees to join Commanders practice squad
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The long rumored landing spot will become a reality for Aiyuk, who was released by the 49ers earlier this week.
item.content:encoded:
Earlier on Wednesday, Brandon Aiyuk's agent, Drew Rosenhaus, told ESPN's Adam Schefter that a decision on whether or not the wideout would join the Commanders was unlikely to happen on Wednesday.

Things have changed.

Schefter now reports Aiyuk has agreed to sign with Washington's practice squad, putting an end to the wideout's long journey to the team.

San Francisco released Aiyuk earlier this week after his roster exemption expired. The receiver cleared waivers and was then free to sign with any franchise.

Aiyuk has not played since 2024.

That year, he played seven games, catching 25 passes.

In his last full season of 2023, he caught 75 passes for 1,342 yards with seven touchdowns.

item.title: Falcons are "aware" of suggestion that James Pearce Jr. has been trying to contact Rickea Jackson
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Falcons defensive end James Pearce Jr. has returned from an eight-game suspension arising from an incident with his former girlfriend, WNBA player Rickea Jackson.
item.content:encoded:
Falcons defensive end James Pearce Jr. has returned from an eight-game suspension arising from an incident with his former girlfriend, WNBA player Rickea Jackson. On Wednesday, coach Kevin Stefanski addressed a suggestion on social media that Pearce has been attempting to contact Jackson, in violation of his plea deal.

"I’m aware," Stefanski told reporters, via Marc Raimondi of ESPN. "We've spoken to James. But we don't have much more to add."

It's not clear that Pearce has been trying to contact Jackson. Her online comments carry a clear implication that she believes "dozens" of calls from a phone number with no ID came from Pearce.

Raimondi also notes that, since his return from suspension, Pearce has not spoken to reporters, declining multiple attempts by the media to question him. League rules require all players to be available after every game and once during the week.

Pearce faces potentially significant consequences if it can be proven that he has violated the terms of his one-year diversion program. Beyond the possibility of an additional suspension, Pearce could face a prison term for the charges that will be dismissed only if he fully complies with the program.

item.title: Jets designate T'Vondre Sweat for return from injured reserve
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Jets will have defensive tackle T'Vondre Sweat back at practice this week.
item.content:encoded:
The Jets will have defensive tackle T'Vondre Sweat back at practice this week.

Sweat has been out since hurting his knee in Week 7, but the Jets announced that he has been designated for return from injured reserve on Wednesday. The move opens up a 21-day practice window and he can be activated at any point in that span.

Sweat joined the Jets in an offseason trade with the Titans. He started six of the team's first seven games this season and had 17 tackles while appearing in every game.

The Jets are coming off of their third win of the season and they'll try for their first winning streak since Weeks 2 and 3 of the 2024 season when they travel to Miami this weekend.

item.title: Marlon Humphrey takes part in Wednesday's Ravens practice
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Cornerback Marlon Humphrey returned to the Ravens' facility on Monday and he returned to their practice field on Wednesday.
item.content:encoded:
Cornerback Marlon Humphrey returned to the Ravens' facility on Monday and he returned to their practice field on Wednesday.

Humphrey was sent home last week and deactivated for the team's loss to the Panthers after saying that Baltimore was the best at "making criminals" on an episode of his podcast. Humphrey apologized for that comment, but was criticized by the city's mayor and many others for the way he characterized local residents.

The Ravens welcomed Humphrey back this week, but head coach Jesse Minter did not commit to playing him in this Sunday's game against the Texans.

Reporters at the open portion of practice also noted that defensive tackle Nnamdi Madubuike and safety Jaylinn Hawkins are not practicing. Both players were out in Week 11.

item.title: Titans sign CB Corey Thornton off of the Panthers practice squad
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Titans have made an addition to their ailing defense.
item.content:encoded:
The Titans have made an addition to their ailing defense.

They announced that they have signed cornerback Corey Thornton off of the Panthers' practice squad. There was no corresponding move needed to clear space for Thornton on the roster in Tennessee.

Thornton appeared in two games for the Panthers this month. He had an interception in their Week 9 loss to the Broncos and also recorded eight tackles and three passes defensed.

After last Sunday's 51-30 loss to the Cowboys, the Titans rank 30th in the league in points allowed and dead last in yards allowed. They'll be hoping Thornton helps them improve on both fronts.

item.title: Brandon Aiyuk finishes visit with Commanders, but decision is not expected on Wednesday
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Brandon Aiyuk may still join the Commanders soon, but it sounds like that's not imminent.
item.content:encoded:
Brandon Aiyuk may still join the Commanders soon, but it sounds like that's not imminent.

Drew Rosenhaus, Aiyuk's agent, said the receiver's visit with Washington is over, via ESPN's Adam Schefter.

Rosenhaus added that “Discussions are ongoing and positive,” but there probably will not be a decision today.

Aiyuk, who has not played since 2024, was released by the 49ers earlier this week and cleared waivers, making him free to sign with any team.

The Commanders have long been thought of as the frontrunner to land Aiyuk

We’ll see if Aiyuk takes more visits before joining a club.

item.description: The Eagles will have cornerback Quinyon Mitchell in the lineup for Thursday's game in Dallas.
item.content:encoded:
The Eagles will have cornerback Quinyon Mitchell in the lineup for Thursday's game in Dallas.

Mitchell did not receive an injury designation for the Thanksgiving game. He was listed as out of practice on Monday due to a hamstring injury, but moved up to limited participation Tuesday and was a full participant on Friday.

Running back Saquon Barkley, defensive tackle Jalen Carter, tight end Dallas Goedert, and wide receiver DeVonta Smith are also without designations after appearing on the injury report this week.

Linebacker Arnold Ebiketie (oblique) and cornerback Jonathan Jones (ankle) are the only players who did receive designations. Both of them have been ruled out for the Eagles this week.

item.title: Panthers designate LB Thomas Incoom for return from IR
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Panthers have opened the practice window for linebacker Thomas Incoom.
item.content:encoded:
The Panthers have opened the practice window for linebacker Thomas Incoom.

Incoom has been designated for return from injured reserve and will be able to practice for the next 21 days as a result. The Panthers can activate him at any point in that window.

Incoom was placed on injured reserve ahead of Week 7 due to a calf injury. He had six tackles and a fumble recovery in five games before his injury.

The Panthers have now designated seven players for return this season. They will be able to do it one more time during the regular season and that spot is expected to be filled by cornerback Jaycee Horn once he is ready to get back on the field.

item.title: PFT's Thanksgiving and Week 12 2026 NFL picks
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: All games picked for one of the most compelling weeks of the season.
item.content:encoded:
It was inevitable.

After flirting a couple of times with landing under .500 in a given week of picks, it finally happened. For Week 11, I went 6-7.

That's what I get for trying to pick upsets. In Week 11, it was Chalk City — and 12 of 13 home teams won.

And so, from now on, I'm not getting cute. I'm sticking with my first impulse. I'm not overthinking it. The first number that pops into my head will be the pick.

For the year, I'm at 102-60-1. The success rate is still 62.5 percent. Here's hoping I can find a way to push it a little higher with the 16 games to be played from Wednesday through Monday.

Packers at Rams (Wednesday night)

Sean McVay is 0-5 against Matt LaFleur. A loss on Wednesday night would put the preseason favorites in grave danger of missing the playoffs, especially in light of an upcoming schedule that includes games against the Chiefs, the 49ers, the Cowboys, the Seahawks (twice), and the Buccaneers.

Rams 24, Packers 20.

Bears at Lions (Thursday)

It's the biggest early-window Thanksgiving game ever, with both teams at 8-2. Ben Johnson's Bears gave up 52 points during last year's visit to Ford Field. They'll be determined to achieve a different result this time, in what becomes a true litmus test for the new-look Bears. If they're truly contenders, this is a game they win.

Bears 23, Lions 21.

Eagles at Cowboys (Thursday)

It won't be a cakewalk. For Philly, it's the closest they'll get this year to a game with a postseason vibe. But the Cowboys have a chance to make a run at the Giants — if Dallas can also hold off the Commanders.

Cowboys 41, Eagles 24.

Chiefs at Bills (Thursday)

Josh Allen is 5-0 against Patrick Mahomes in the regular season, 0-4 against Mahomes in the postseason. The trend continues, thanks to conditions that are more conducive to Allen making the right throw at the right time.

Bills 23, Chiefs 17.

Broncos at Steelers (Friday)

This one had the feel of a game the Steelers would find a way to win, until the benching of Aaron Rodgers threw everything into disarray.

Broncos 20, Steelers 13.

Saints at Bengals

The Bengals need to get back on track, quickly, after Monday night's sluggish performance. A slump could open the door for the Browns to steal the division.

Bengals 31, Saints 20.

Ravens at Texans

It feels like an elimination game in Houston, even if the winner will still be facing an uphill climb to the postseason. When in doubt, ride with the clearly better quarterback.

Texans 27, Ravens 23.

Giants at Colts

This will be a far cry from the 1958 NFL Championship. The Giants are surging, and the Colts are slowly disintegrating.

Giants 24, Colts 9.

Titans at Jaguars

As the saying goes, it's not the size of the dog in the fight but the size of the fight in the dog. Unfortunately, this fight is round two of Doberman vs. Chihuahua.

Jaguars 35, Titans 20.

Jets at Dolphins

The Dolphins are running out of chances to get a second win (if they even want one).

Dolphins 23, Jets 13.

Falcons at Vikings

Kirk Cousins gets the double whammy — his first home game in his second stint with the Vikings, and his first shot at revenge against the team that signed him and then drafted his replacement.

Vikings 27, Falcons 13.

Patriots at Chargers

It's fitting that a game pitting two struggling teams coached by former Ohio State and Michigan players happens one day after a game between struggling Ohio State and Michigan teams.

Patriots 16, Chargers 10.

Commanders at Cardinals

Monday night's upset of the Bengals means nothing if the Commanders bungle a winnable game at Arizona.

Commanders 27, Cardinals 10.

Seahawks at 49ers

Having an extra week to prepare, coupled with the urgency of a 6-4 record, is just what the doctor ordered for the Seahawks.

Seahawks 27, 49ers 23.

Raiders at Browns

The NFL will be happy it flexed this one into primetime. (For reasons other than getting Patriots-Chargers out of that window.)

Browns 30, Raiders 27.

Panthers at Buccaneers

Tampa Bay is running out of chances to pull themselves back into contention.

Buccaneers 27, Panthers 20.

item.title: Devontez Walker wins AFC special teams player of the week
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Ravens didn’t beat the Panthers on Sunday, but they did have one individual do enough to win a player of the week award.
item.content:encoded:
The Ravens didn’t beat the Panthers on Sunday, but they did have one individual do enough to win a player of the week award.

The NFL named returner Devontez Walker special teams player of the week.

Walker had an 86-yard kickoff return for a touchdown in the second quarter of the contest. He ended up returning seven kicks for 211 yards, becoming the second player to have at least 200 kickoff return yards in a game this season.

His touchdown return was just the second kick returned for a TD this season.

This is Walker’s first player of the week award.

item.title: Abdul Carter wins first NFC defensive player of the week award
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Giants edge rusher Abdul Carter was a game wrecker during Sunday's victory over the Jaguars.
item.content:encoded:
Giants edge rusher Abdul Carter was a game wrecker during Sunday's victory over the Jaguars.

Now he's been named NFC defensive player of the week.

Carter had four tackles with 2.0 sacks in the 23-18 victory. The NFL notes that according to Next Gen Stats, Carter had 12 QB pressures in Week 11, which is the second most recorded in a single game this season.

This is Carter’s first defensive player of the week award.

Carter now has 4.0 sacks, five tackles for loss, and 13 quarterback hits this season.

item.title: Commanders K Drew Stevens is the NFC special teams player of the week
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Commanders called on kicker Drew Stevens often in Week 11 and he came through each and every time.
item.content:encoded:
The Commanders called on kicker Drew Stevens often in Week 11 and he came through each and every time.

Stevens was asked to attempt field goals at the end of all five of Washington's possessions in the second half of their home date with the Bengals and Stevens made all five of those kicks. The last of them came on the final snap of the game and the 26-yard kick gave the Commanders a 22-20 win.

Stevens was named the NFC special teams player of the week on Wednesday.

The Commanders signed Stevens as an undrafted rookie this offseason and he is now 22-of-25 on field goals and 16-of-19 on extra points on the year.

item.title: Will Anderson named the AFC defensive player of the week
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Texans hurt their playoff chances with a slow start to the regular season, but they are still in the hunt and having defensive end Will Anderson will help their chances.
item.content:encoded:
The Texans hurt their playoff chances with a slow start to the regular season, but they are still in the hunt and having defensive end Will Anderson will help their chances.

Anderson helped them to their fourth win in the last six games last Thursday by recording five tackles, a sack, two tackles for loss and four quarterback hits against the Colts. Anderson's sack of Daniel Jones came in the end zone for the first sack of the Texans pass rusher's career.

The NFL named Anderson the AFC defensive player of the week on Wednesday. It's the second time he's won the award in his career.

Anderson leads the league with 11.5 sacks and the Texans' postseason hopes will keep improving as long as he continues to produce off the edge on defense.

item.title: Brock Purdy wins fourth career NFC offensive player of the week award
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Brock Purdy is an MVP candidate and had another strong performance in Sunday’s victory over the Vikings.
item.content:encoded:
Brock Purdy is an MVP candidate and had another strong performance in Sunday’s victory over the Vikings.

Now he’s been named NFC offensive player of the week.

Purdy finished the game 21-of-26 passing for 255 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions — good for a 146.0 passer rating.

This was Purdy’s seventh career game with a passer rating of at least 145, which is the most by a player in his first five seasons in league history.

Purdy is one of two quarterbacks with a passer rating of at least 100 in eight games this season, the other being Cincinnati’s Joe Burrow.

Purdy has now won four career offensive player of the week awards.

The current No. 1 seed in the conference, Purdy and the 49ers will host the Seahawks on Sunday afternoon.

item.title: Jonah Coleman is the AFC offensive player of the week
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Broncos rookie Jonah Coleman has moved to the top of the running back depth chart in Denver since returning from injured reserve late last month and he had his biggest game yet against the Raiders in Week 11.
item.content:encoded:
Broncos rookie Jonah Coleman has moved to the top of the running back depth chart in Denver since returning from injured reserve late last month and he had his biggest game yet against the Raiders in Week 11.

Coleman ran 24 times for 111 yards and three touchdowns to help the Broncos to a 38-24 win. Those were all season-highs for Coleman, who now has five touchdowns in the last three weeks.

The NFL named Coleman the AFC offensive player of the week in recognition of that effort.

Coleman is the first Bronco to win the award since quarterback Bo Nix at the end of the 2024 season and the Broncos will be hoping that the duo is just at the start of a fruitful partnership.

item.title: Kenneth Walker ruled out for Thanksgiving night vs. Bills
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Rookie RB Emmett Johnson is now set to start his third consecutive game.
item.content:encoded:
The Chiefs will not have Kenneth Walker when they play the Bills on Thursday.

Kansas City has officially ruled Walker out for the contest, putting rookie Emmett Johnson in line to start for the third consecutive game.

Walker (groin) returned to practice on Tuesday in a limited capacity. But Walker would not have practiced on Wednesday and won’t play against Buffalo.

Walker has used for 872 yards with seven touchdowns in eight games. He still leads the league averaging 5.5 yards per carry. He’s also caught 26 passes for 172 yards with four touchdowns.

Johnson, a rookie fifth-round pick, has rushed for 100 yards in each of the last two games. In Sunday’s win over the Cardinals, he had 105 yards on 23 carries with a touchdown and four catches for 38 yards.

The Chiefs also ruled out right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) and defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (knee).

Tight end Noah Gray (rib) and defensive lineman Peter Woods (neck) are questionable.

Cornerback Mansoor Delane (shoulder), receiver Rashee Rice (knee), guard Trey Smith (concussion), and quarterback Patrick Mahomes (knee/right elbow) are all off the injury report and are set to play.

item.title: Report: Steelers were changing the play-calling process as of Tuesday
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: More and more information is emerging as to the surprise decision to bench Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers.
item.content:encoded:
More and more information is emerging as to the surprise decision to bench Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers.

Here's an interesting nugget, from Mike Garafolo of NFL Network.

As Garafolo explains it, the Steelers were changing their play-calling process. Starting Friday, quarterbacks coach Tom Arth, not head coach Mike McCarthy, would have been communicating the plays to Rodgers.

Previously, Arth handled play-calling during the two-minute drill. Moving forward, Arth would have been doing it for the entire game.

They worked on the new approach at practice on Tuesday. It was something Rodgers wanted.

At some point, that changed. McCarthy opted to bench Rodgers instead.

The situation dusts off the drama from nearly eight weeks ago, when Rodgers and McCarthy's on-field unpleasantries during a loss to the Browns flowed from Rodgers's frustrations regarding the pace of McCarthy's play calls.

And it suggests that Tuesday's move was simply the last domino in a chain that started falling the moment Rodgers shouted, "What the fuck? Call it!" and McCarthy responded by saying, "Fucking asshole."

item.title: Jalen McMillan to return to practice for the Buccaneers
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Wide receiver Jalen McMillan is on his way back to the Buccaneers lineup.
item.content:encoded:
Wide receiver Jalen McMillan is on his way back to the Buccaneers lineup.

Greg Auman of Fox Sports reports that McMillan will return to practice on Wednesday. The move will start the clock on his 21-day window to practice before he must be activated from injured reserve or shut down for the year.

McMillan can be activated at any point in that window. He has been out since injuring his knee in Week 3 and he did not catch any passes in his two appearances this season.

Auman reports that linebacker Christian Rozeboom is also being designated for return after missing five games with a finger injury. He had 11 tackles in the first five games of the year.

item.description: The five-game football feast surrounding Thanksgiving has major playoff implications for all 10 teams playing around the holiday.
item.content:encoded:
The five-game football feast surrounding Thanksgiving has major playoff implications for all 10 teams playing around the holiday. We look at the playoff race for Week 12 below:

AFC Playoff Picture

DIVISION LEADERS

1. Bills (9-1): Will have the inside track for the No. 1 seed if they win on Thanksgiving night against the Chiefs.

2. Broncos (8-2): Currently ahead of the Chiefs in the AFC West based on the better record in common games

3. Jaguars (7-3): Loss to the Giants was a big blow to their hopes of earning the No. 1 seed in the AFC.

4. Bengals (7-3): In control of the AFC North, but Monday night's loss in Washington hurts.

WILD CARDS

5. Chiefs (8-2): Huge game coming against the Bills on Thanksgiving night.

6. Browns (6-4): Cleveland's path to the playoffs is looking surprisingly easy.

7. Steelers (6-4): Major questions about the direction of this team after benching Aaron Rodgers.

OUTSIDE LOOKING IN

8. Patriots (5-5): Hard to see them competing without Drake Maye.

9. Texans (4-6): Running out of time to go on a run.

10 Raiders (4-7): The rest of the season is about developing Fernando Mendoza.

11. Ravens (4-7): Lamar Jackson's injury just about killed their playoff hopes.

12. Jets (3-8): Aaron Glenn is on the hot seat.

13. Colts (3-8): No longer competing.

14. Chargers (1-9): The NFL's most disappointing team.

15. Dolphins (1-9): The playoffs this year were never a realistic possibility.

16. Titans (1-9): Need to figure out if Cam Ward is their quarterback.

NFC Playoff Picture

DIVISION LEADERS

1. 49ers (9-1): Inside track for the No. 1 seed after a big win Sunday night against the Vikings.

2. Lions (8-2): First place in the NFC North is on the line in the Thanksgiving showdown with the Bears.

3. Giants (6-3-1): Clear path to the playoffs in John Harbaugh's first season.

4. Panthers (5-5): Best record in the NFL's worst division.

WILD CARDS

5. Bears (8-2): They'll lead the division if they beat the Lions on Thanksgiving, but if they lose they'll be 0-3 in the NFC North.

6. Vikings (7-3): Have lost three of their last four after a hot start.

7. Packers (6-4): Big game on Thanksgiving Eve against the Rams.

OUTSIDE LOOKING IN

8. Seahawks (6-4): Currently have the tiebreaker edge over the Rams, but those two teams still play each other twice.

9. Rams (6-4): Big game on Thanksgiving Eve against the Packers.

10. Cowboys (5-6): It won't be easy to catch the Giants in the NFC East.

11. Commanders (4-5-1): May need to run the table to win the division.

12. Buccaneers (3-7): Still in the race in the terrible NFC South.

13. Falcons (3-7): Still in the race in the terrible NFC South.

14. Saints (3-7): Still in the race in the terrible NFC South.

15. Eagles (3-7): Showed some fight in upsetting the Steelers.

16. Cardinals (3-8): Worst team in the NFC.

item.title: Dolphins sign P Jack Browning to their 53-man roster
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Dolphins added a second punter to their 53-man roster on Wednesday.
item.content:encoded:
The Dolphins added a second punter to their 53-man roster on Wednesday.

They announced that they have signed Jack Browning off of their practice squad. The Dolphins had an open spot, so there was no corresponding move needed to sign Browning.

Browning was elevated for last Sunday's loss to the Bills because Bradley Pinion was out with a groin injury. Wednesday's move suggests he'll be handling the punting and holding duties against the Jets this weekend as well.

Browning punted four times for 165 yards against Buffalo. One of those punts landed inside the 20-yard-line.

The Dolphins also announced that they have signed defensive end Max Llewellyn to the practice squad. Llewellyn was waived off the 53-man roster earlier this week.

item.title: Jaguars open practice window for OL Patrick Mekari
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Jaguars are getting a key player back on the practice field.
item.content:encoded:
The Jaguars are getting a key player back on the practice field.

Jacksonville has opened the 21-day practice window for offensive lineman Patrick Mekari, the team announced on Wednesday.

Mekari was placed on injured reserve with a designation to return at roster cuts in August. He had undergone offseason back surgery.

Mekari started 14 games at right guard for the Jaguars last season.

He joined the club on a three-year deal in the 2025 offseason after spending his first six seasons with the Ravens.

item.title: Report: Aaron Rodgers was "excused" from work on Wednesday
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The sudden, late-night benching of quarterback Aaron Rodgers has created a slew of questions that are being answered in real time.
item.content:encoded:
The sudden, late-night benching of quarterback Aaron Rodgers has created a slew of questions that are being answered in real time.

One of the obvious questions was answered on Wednesday morning, when Gerry Dulac of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette reported that Rodgers didn’t show up for work on Wednesday. Implicit in that report was the idea that he chose to no-show.

Now, Adam Schefter of ESPN reports that Rodgers's absence was "excused" as he processes the fact that coach Mike McCarthy has decided to play Mason Rudolph on Friday against the Broncos.

At some point, Rodgers will have something to say. Maybe he'll make a surprise appearance on McAfee's show today, even if that development would surprise no one.

Rodgers will surely have an opinion on the situation. Chances are that his opinion will be something other than, "You know, they were right to bench me."

We've seen this movie before. Rodgers has no qualms about airing grievances. Now, the Steelers have given him a specific reason to feel aggrieved.

The surprise at this point wouldn't be Rodgers showing up on McAfee's show and flaming the Steelers. The surprise would be Rodgers saying nothing.

Silence could easily be interpreted as acceptance of, and possibly agreement with, the move. Beyond that, Rodgers has shown (specifically since his 2021 heel turn) that he's never silent on topics about which he has strong feelings.

item.title: Kenneth Walker limited in his return to Chiefs practice
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Walker missed the last two games with a groin injury.
item.content:encoded:
Chiefs head coach Andy Reid said he expected running back Kenneth Walker back at practice on Tuesday and the team's injury report confirmed that Walker was a limited participant.

Walker has missed the last two games with a groin injury, but his return to work would seem to open the door to a return to the lineup against the Bills on Thursday night.

Walker ran 159 times for 872 yards and seven touchdowns in eight games before the injury. He also has 26 catches for 172 yards and four touchdowns.

Tight end Noah Gray also returned to practice which left right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) was the only Chief out of practice. Defensive tackle Omarr Norman-Lott (knee) was listed as limited while Gray (rib), cornerback Mansoor Delane (shoulder), wide receiver Rashee Rice (knee), right guard Trey Smith (concussion), and defensive lineman Peter Woods (neck) were full participants.

item.title: PFT's Week 12 2026 NFL power rankings
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The 49ers can no longer be denied the top spot.
item.content:encoded:
1. 49ers (last week No. 3; 9-1): They made the best defense in the NFL look like the worst.

2. Bills (No. 1; 9-1): They're beating overmatched teams, but the wins are becoming less impressive.

3. Broncos (No. 4; 8-2): They need to start playing on the road the way they play at home.

4. Bears (No. 5; 8-2): We'll learn a lot about this team in Detroit on Thursday.

5. Chiefs (No. 6; 8-2): They're making it look easy, just like they used to.

6. Jaguars (No. 2; 7-3): They need to figure out how to win when it's not coming easily.

7. Lions (No. 9; 8-2): Can they slow down Chicago's offense? We're about to find out.

8. Bengals (No. 7; 7-3): A championship-caliber franchise doesn't choke against a team that is below .500.

9. Seahawks (No. 8; 6-4): The season may come down to whether they can win in San Francisco.

10. Giants (No. 15; 6-3-1): John Harbaugh has quickly remade this franchise in his image.

11. Vikings (No. 10; 7-3): With five of their last seven games at home, they're very much alive for the division title.

12. Rams (No. 12; 6-4): Wednesday night's visit from the Packers could be a de facto playoff game.

13. Packers (No. 13; 6-4): Can Micah Parsons make the difference?

14. Browns (No. 14; 6-4): Forget clinging to the seventh seed — the No. 6 seed is there for the taking.

15. Steelers (No. 11; 6-4): Playoffs or not, the Steelers aren't good enough to compete with the best teams in the AFC.

16. Panthers (No. 17; 5-5): Somehow, an NFC South team has gotten to .500.

17. Commanders (No. 21; 4-5-1): For the second time in three years, Jayden Daniels outdueled Joe Burrow in prime time.

18. Patriots (No. 16; 5-5): If they can't beat the Chargers, they've got no chance to get back to the playoffs.

19. Texans (No. 22; 4-6): C.J. Stroud is back. Will the defense ever be able to say the same thing?

20. Cowboys (No. 24; 5-6): The score-on-every-drive approach to offsetting a bad defense will only take them so far.

21. Raiders (No. 18; 4-7): The foundation is being laid for Fernando Mendoza to elevate the franchise in 2027.

22. Buccaneers (No. 19; 3-7): Monday night's visit from the Panthers could be an elimination game.

23. Ravens (No. 20; 4-7): Sunday's visit to the Texans is an elimination game.

24. Eagles (No. 28; 3-7): Playing for pride is going to screw up their draft position.

25. Saints (No. 23; 3-7): Time may be running out for Kellen Moore.

26. Falcons (No. 26; 3-7): They'd be better off if Sunday's game at Minnesota had been moved to prime time.

27. Jets (No. 32; 3-8): The win over the Chargers delays the inevitable coaching change.

28. Cardinals (No. 25; 3-8): At least they get 1/32nd of the shared NFL revenue.

29. Colts (No. 27; 3-8): For the past year, every big decision they've made has been the wrong one.

30. Chargers (No. 29; 1-9): Will Jim Harbaugh be back for 2027?

31. Titans (No. 30; 1-9): With franchise values increasing, doesn't it make sense for ownership to consider cashing out and moving on?

32. Dolphins (No. 31; 1-9): With the Jets coming to town, the Dolphins have one of their last, best chances to get another win.

item.title: Bears-Lions is first Thanksgiving game ever with both teams on 5+ game winning streaks
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: One of the best Thanksgiving games ever will take place Thursday in Detroit.
item.content:encoded:
One of the best Thanksgiving games ever will take place Thursday in Detroit.

When the Lions host the Bears, it will be the first time in NFL history that two teams on winning streaks of five games or longer meet on Thanksgiving. The Lions are on a six-game winning streak and the Bears are on a five-game winning streak.

The Lions and Bears are both 8-2 and tied for first place in the NFC North, so the game has major playoff implications. The winner will be all alone in first place in the best division in football.

This will be the 21st time the Bears and Lions have met on Thanksgiving. The Bears have an 11-9 edge in the previous 20 games.

item.title: Ben Johnson: D'Andre Swift doesn't need to regain trust after fumble
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Bears running back D'Andre Swift did not return to last Sunday's game after losing a fumble in the fourth quarter and his role moving forward was a topic at head coach Ben Johnson's press conference on Tuesday.
item.content:encoded:
Bears running back D'Andre Swift did not return to last Sunday's game after losing a fumble in the fourth quarter and his role moving forward was a topic at head coach Ben Johnson's press conference on Tuesday.

Swift has now lost three fumbles this season and he's spent time on the bench after two of them, which made it natural that Johnson fielded a question about whether the back needs to regain the trust of the coaching staff. Johnson said that is not the case.

"Nope. He just needs to hold on to the ball and we'll be fine," Johnson said.

Swift had 51 yards on 13 carries against the Saints and is averaging 3.7 yards per carry on the season and the Bears backs have been less efficient running the ball since a 232-yard game against the Jets in Week 4. The Bears have still won five of their last six games, but finding a way to be more productive on the ground would be a good way to keep the wins coming in a competitive race for playoff positions in the NFC.

item.title: Aaron Rodgers could land, in time, on reserve/left squad list
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: As real-time drama unfolds for the Steelers and quarterback Aaron Rodgers, the situation could play out in various ways.
item.content:encoded:
As real-time drama unfolds for the Steelers and quarterback Aaron Rodgers, the situation could play out in various ways.

For now, his reported failure to show up for work on Wednesday could eventually result in his placement on the reserve/left squad list.

The first step would be for the Steelers to send Rodges what's known as a "five-day letter." If/when the letter is sent and if/when he doesn't return within five days, the Steelers would be able to shift him to the reserve/left squad list.

That would shut him down for the rest of the season. He couldn't play for the Steelers, and he couldn't play for anyone else. He'd be stuck in that category indefinitely and at least until 2027. Given that he has repeatedly said that he won't play after the 2026 season, that's how his career could end.

It's still early in the process. He could ask to be released, and the Steelers could grant it. If they refuse — and if he doesn't return — reserve/left squad becomes a viable option.
